title: Jack & the Beanstalk
strapline: Plant a magic bean and climb up into the clouds.
intent: A story about a bean that grows to the sky links naturally to real planting, growth and the wonder of change over time.
Climbing high, giant footsteps and 'Fee, fi, fo, fum' give children big language, big movement and a refrain to chant.
The giant's castle in the clouds is a rich small world for building high, hiding and daring adventure.
Swapping a cow for beans opens gentle talk about value, choices and whether it was a good idea.
Comparing tiny bean to enormous beanstalk to giant stretches size and measure language.
implementation: Set out Jack, the cow, magic beans, a beanstalk to build tall and a castle in the clouds with a giant.
Tell the story with a booming giant voice and a big 'Fee, fi, fo, fum', then hand the play over.
Plant real beans alongside the story and watch them climb — measuring and marking growth each day.
Wonder together: 'How tall could this beanstalk grow? How could we measure it?'
Bring in the value talk: 'Was swapping the cow for beans a good idea? What do you think?'
Follow the children — some will build ever-taller beanstalks and towers, others will play the giant's castle.
key_questions: How tall do you think the beanstalk could grow — how could we measure it?
What did Jack find at the top?
Was it a good idea to swap the cow for beans?
Can you stomp and roar like the giant?
What does a bean need to grow so big?

impact.text: Children plant beans and observe, measure and talk about their growth over time.
Children build tall structures and compare heights using size language.
Children chant the giant's refrain and retell the adventure.
Children talk about Jack's choices and whether the swap was wise.
Children play out the castle adventure with roles and shared storylines.

enhancements: A real bean-planting station — broad beans in clear jars so roots and shoots are visible — measured daily.
A tall-tower or beanstalk building challenge: how high can it go before it topples?
A giant's castle small world in the clouds with cotton-wool sky and a golden harp and hen.
Giant footprints and a measuring station — how many of my feet fit in the giant's?
Golden-egg or golden-coin counting and sorting from the giant's treasure.

playing_exploring: Children plant, climb, stomp and roar, living the story with their bodies.
They watch real beans sprout and climb, checking on them with fascination.
active_learning: Children keep building taller, solving how to stop the tower toppling.
They tend and measure their beans patiently over the weeks.
creating_thinking: Children reason about height and growth and predict how tall things will get.
They debate whether the swap was wise and invent their own adventures up the beanstalk.
